editorial.headline: Architecture Beyond the Drawing Board
editorial.standfirst: This activity spans architectural advice, design and planning—from buildings and landscapes to urban land use—with national foreign ownership open to 100% and no Bali moratorium block.
editorial.body:
Architectural activity here is not confined to producing drawings for a single building. It covers the full advisory and design terrain of architectural practice: early architectural studies, pre-design advice, architectural design and other architectural services, as well as assessments of a building’s maintenance and feasibility. Its reach extends from the individual building to the spaces around it—built environments, landscapes, regions and urban areas—and includes work on the use and development of space.

The scope is equally concerned with how the built environment is shaped over time. It includes designing buildings and their surroundings, planning the conservation of buildings and their environments, and preparing arrangements for buildings and their settings. It also includes technical planning documents and supervision of architectural aspects during construction. Urban planning, land-use planning, project management, construction management, community assistance and other construction-related work are expressly within the activity’s stated scope.

Its building-design remit is broad, covering objects classified across meeting and assembly, business, education, factories and industrial buildings, high-hazard buildings, institutional and government uses, commercial premises, homes, storage, utilities and miscellaneous buildings. The activity is open at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scale. Nationally, it is classified as open to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. **For this activity, Bali does not turn a nationally open architectural practice into a barred foreign-investment registration.**

That Bali conclusion rests on the record’s stated risk position at the Large scale: the OSS risk is medium-high or high, so the activity is not blocked by the provincial moratorium. The moratorium itself blocks all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities for PMA across the province on a permanent, island-wide basis. That rule does not produce a block here. The practical reading is therefore straightforward: the activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, and its Bali status is not blocked by that moratorium, with the recorded Large-scale risk classification explaining why.
